items.claim: The row's rejected_alternative claims no content token links web:Eccl.6.3-Eccl.6.6 to oshb:Eccl.6.2, but the hevel root occurs on both sides of the row's own front seam, undisclosed as cross-seam cohesion.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.6.2 closes on the bare token הֶ֛בֶל ("hevel"), and oshb:Eccl.6.4 -- inside this row's own span -- opens its causal clause with the prefixed form בַהֶ֥בֶל ("ba-hevel"); both are hevel-family tokens (sweep: hevel-family 30 verses / 38 tokens book-wide, eccl_device_inventory.json hevel_refrain). The row's strongest_rejected_alternative states flatly that "no content token links it to oshb:Eccl.6.2's alien-eats-it case" -- that specific claim is false as stated. The scenario-shift argument (a new conditional "if a man fathers..." case) may still be the stronger reading of the seam, but the row should disclose and argue past the hevel echo rather than deny it exists.

items.claim: The maxim-to-refrain span at web:Eccl.6.7-Eccl.6.9 is well warranted on both boundaries: a fresh generalizing maxim opens with no token shared with 6.6's close, and the row's own reut-ruach refrain closes the unit before the register shift at 6.10.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.6.7 opens כָּל עֲמַ֥ל..., sharing no token with 6.6's closing question, and oshb:Eccl.6.9 closes זֶ֥ה הֶ֖בֶל וּרְע֥וּת רֽוּחַ, one of the inventory's 7 reut-ruach sites; 6.10's naming/contention vocabulary shares nothing with 6.9. No undisclosed cross-seam device found at either edge of this row.

items.claim: The English gloss for oshb:Eccl.6.12 splices two separate WEB sentences into one quotation via an ellipsis, so the Hebrew and English quotations do not share the same span, and the verse's own hevel-family token plus its tachat-hashemesh close are both left undisclosed.
items.evidence: WEB Eccl.6.12 is two sentences: “For who knows what is good for man in life, all the days of his vain life which he spends like a shadow? For who can tell a man what will be after him under the sun?” The row quotes only “who knows what is good for man in life…under the sun?”, welding sentence one's opening to sentence two's closing and skipping the intervening material -- including oshb:Eccl.6.12's own suffixed hevel-family token הֶבְל֖וֹ ("his vanity") and the verse's close תַּ֥חַת הַשָּֽׁמֶשׁ ("under the sun", one of 27 tachat-hashemesh sites) -- while the row's own Hebrew quotation stops at חַיֵּ֥י, short of both. Quote and gloss must share a span; here the English covers material the Hebrew never quotes, and the elided material is exactly the two refrain-bearing tokens this row's "hinge to web:Eccl.7.1" framing should have weighed but never names in device_notes.

items.claim: The saying_cluster at web:Eccl.7.2-Eccl.7.4 is byte-grounded, not thin: the house-of-mourning phrase recurs verbatim at the cluster's open and close bracketing a causally-linked middle verse, and the rejected_alternative correctly names and argues past the wider 7.1-7.8 tov-anaphora rival with real, byte-checkable gaps.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.2 carries בֵּֽית אֵ֗בֶל and oshb:Eccl.7.4 carries בְּבֵ֣ית אֵ֔בֶל ("house of mourning") -- the same two-word construct pair bracketing the cluster, once in a motion-to construction and once in a locative construction, so the recurrence is exact at the skeleton/consonantal tier and each quote is byte-accurate to its own cited verse, though the two surface forms differ by the locative prefix and by position-conditioned pointing (not byte-identical to each other). This brackets 7.3's own causal clause on the same mourning/mirth axis; the wider-cluster rival is correctly rejected on the real point that 7.1 and 7.5 share no phrase with the bracket and 7.7 breaks the tov-opener run with unrelated corruption vocabulary.

items.claim: The saying_cluster at web:Eccl.7.5-Eccl.7.6 is warranted by a genuine causal dependency closed on the book's own hevel tag, and this row is the one place in the cluster that correctly discloses and argues past shared vocabulary with a neighbor rather than denying it.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.6 opens with a causal clause explaining 7.5's tov-saying and closes on the hevel tag, one of the inventory's hevel sites; the row's rejected_alternative explicitly names the shared wise/fool vocabulary with 7.4 (the token חָכָ֑ם recurs again at 7.7, see p02-015) and argues past it on the grounds that 7.4 belongs to its own closed phrase-bracket -- the correct disclosure move, and a useful contrast to the undisclosed echoes found elsewhere in this cluster.

items.claim: The claim that web:Eccl.7.7 "shares no content token with the fool's-laughter pair before it" is false: 7.7 and 7.5 carry the byte-identical token "wise", an undisclosed vocabulary echo across the row's own front seam.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.5 and oshb:Eccl.7.7 both carry the identical pointed token חָכָ֑ם ("wise"), yet the row's boundary_rationale states the verse "shares no content token with the fool's-laughter pair before it." The single_saying atomic verdict is still defensible on its own terms (7.7's corruption/bribery topic differs from 7.5-7.6's hearing-preference topic, and the sentence zone's default is atomic), but the specific no-shared-token claim should be corrected rather than asserted as stated.

items.claim: Two device-notes defects at web:Eccl.7.8: the claim of "no repeated phrase... with the anger-admonition after it" misses that 7.8's own ruach vocabulary is picked up by 7.9, and the tov-opener count double-counts 7.8 against an inventory whose count_object is verse-initial only.
items.evidence: oshb:Eccl.7.8 carries two ruach tokens (ר֖וּחַ, רֽוּחַ) and oshb:Eccl.7.9 opens with בְּרֽוּחֲךָ֖ ("in your spirit"), the same root -- undisclosed by the row's claim of no shared phrase with "the anger-admonition after it." Separately, device_notes' "oshb:Eccl.7.8 (5th and 6th of 7 in-chapter sites)" misapplies the inventory's own count_object ("verses whose first skeleton token is tov"): only the verse-initial ט֛וֹב (token index 0) qualifies under that definition; the second ט֥וֹב sits at token index 4, not verse-initial, so 7.8 is the 5th of 7 sites, not two of them, and crediting one verse with two sites against a stated 7-site total is internally inconsistent. Neither defect overturns the single_saying verdict (one grammatically complete verse, correctly undivided), but both misrepresent the tier-1 sweep objects the row itself cites.
